newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Up on tight supplies, demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Up on tight supplies, demand.

text.p: Increased buying interest emerged in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Wednesday amid tighter supplies from the Middle East during the upcoming summer season, traders said.
The SIMEX futures contract also followed the uptrend momentum, with June and July both up $1.30 to $101.50 and $100.50 respectively.
A few bids for the 180-cst grade were heard at $101.00 per tonne then later rose to $102.00 but suppliers were unwilling to offer, traders said.
On Tuesday, the 180-cst grade was traded at $101.00 per tonne for delivery between May 28 and June 1, compared with the previous traded level at $102.00.
"Prices should go up if you look at the fundamental side. There is no reason for the 180-cst to fall on Tuesday," said one trader.
Talk that two to three Middle East cargoes committed to a local trader would arrive sooner than expected aided the uptrend momentum, traders said.
"There are worries that if they don't buy today, they will have to pay a lot more later," said another trader, noting speculation that the local trader would bid up the market.

While supplies are expected to decrease seasonally from the Middle East, Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) on Wednesday issued a tender to buy at least one 38,000-tonne cargo of 0.5-percent fuel oil for July 1-20 delivery.
The market is also watching results for two fuel oil tenders, expected at the end of the week, from South Korea and Taiwan.

The Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO) tendered to buy two 70,000-tonne cargoes of 0.3-percent 540-centistoke fuel oil for July delivery while Taiwan tendered to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent fuel oil for June lifting on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
